title: Localize a filtered ring diagram at a local target
statement: Let $J$ be a small filtered category and $D:J\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ a diagram [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $T$ be a nontrivial commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal and $g:\operatorname{colim}D\to T$ a ring map presenting $T$ as the localization at a submonoid $W$ (the elements of $W$ map to units, all target elements are fractions, and equality of base elements is detected after multiplication by an element of $W$). Then there exist a diagram $B:J\to\mathrm{CommRing}$, a colimit cocone $\beta:B\to T$, and a natural transformation $\iota_B:D\to B$. Every component of $\iota_B$ is essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], every component of $\beta$ reflects units, and $\beta_i\circ(\iota_B)_i=g\circ\iota_i$ for each canonical colimit leg $\iota_i$.

source.place: Tag 037D (lemma-colimit-normal-ring), first paragraph of the proof, localization at contracted primes; Tag 00QV (lemma-limit-essentially-finite-presentation), final paragraph, localization at the inverse-image prime.

proof.text: Let q be the inverse image under g of the maximal ideal of T. It is prime. Each original denominator maps to a unit, and every element outside q maps to a unit, so IsLocalization.of_le enlarges W to q.primeCompl. IsLocalization.algEquiv uniquely identifies the canonical localization at q with T.

Apply filteredColimitLocalizationAtPrime to D and q, obtaining the localized diagram B, its object identifications, its compatible localization maps, and a colimit cocone whose point is the canonical localization at q.

Use the object identifications to assemble the localization maps into a natural transformation ιB. Compose the cocone with its point identification and the localization algebra equivalence to T. IsColimit.extendIso gives the resulting colimit cocone β. The localization compatibility and the algebra-equivalence equation give βᵢ ∘ ιBᵢ = g ∘ ιᵢ.

A localization map is essentially of finite type by Algebra.EssFiniteType.of_isLocalization. Composition with the object equivalence preserves this. For locality, precompose βᵢ with the inverse object equivalence and use localization extensionality on the original ring: it equals the canonical localRingHom at the contracted prime followed by the equivalence to T. Localization.isLocalHom_localRingHom and the locality of ring equivalences give locality of βᵢ.

theorem exists_localized_filtered_ring_system
    {J : Type u} [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J]
    (D : J ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (T : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsLocalRing T]
    (g : (colimit D : CommRingCat.{u}) →+* T) (W : Submonoid (colimit D : CommRingCat.{u}))
    (hT : letI := g.toAlgebra; IsLocalization W T) :
    ∃ (B : J ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (β : B ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj T) (ιB : D ⟶ B),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk T β)) ∧
      (∀ i, (ιB.app i).hom.EssFiniteType) ∧
      (∀ i, IsLocalHom (β.app i).hom) ∧
      (∀ i, (β.app i).hom.comp (ιB.app i).hom = g.comp (colimit.ι D i).hom)
